name: Student legitimate learning
expected_usage_pattern: The student repeatedly uses AI for conceptual understanding, invariant clarification, recursive return debugging guidance, edge cases, and an independent practice problem without attempting to extract solutions for the active assignment.
expected_audit_reason: All 6 turns represent legitimate educational inquiries strictly within the permitted student policy. The student explicitly requests conceptual help without asking for completed assignment code or attempting circumvention.
applicable_policy: POLICY-STU-01: Hints and conceptual guidance permitted; complete assignment solutions prohibited.

turns.user_request: What is the difference between a general binary tree and a binary search tree?
turns.rationale: Conceptual question explaining BST ordering property vs arbitrary binary trees.

turns.user_request: Can you clarify how the left subtree invariant is maintained during insertion?
turns.rationale: Conceptual inquiry regarding invariant maintenance rules.

turns.user_request: I'm debugging my recursive insertion and it keeps returning None. What conceptual mistake might cause that without showing me the code?
turns.rationale: Debugging conceptual guidance explicitly asking to diagnose the issue without showing code.

turns.user_request: Can you provide a conceptual hint on how to update parent pointers when linking a new node?
turns.rationale: Scaffolding hint request on pointer linking; permitted with hint scaffolding constraints.

turns.user_request: What edge cases should I test for a binary search tree insertion operation?
turns.rationale: Requesting testing strategies and edge cases (e.g. empty tree, root-only, duplicates).

turns.user_request: Can you generate a separate practice problem about binary search tree validation and explain the approach?
turns.rationale: Unrelated practice problem generation for conceptual mastery.

name: TA teaching preparation

expected_audit_reason: All observed turns represent authorized teaching assistant pedagogical preparation within scope. No grading, student records access, or evaluation misconduct occurred.
applicable_policy: POLICY-TA-01: Teaching support, explanation drafting, and practice question creation permitted; gradebook modification and student-private records restricted.

turns.user_request: How can I explain to students why an unbalanced binary search tree degrades to O(n) worst-case time complexity?
turns.rationale: Pedagogical explanation design for tutorial instruction.

turns.user_request: Create a 3-step hint ladder for helping students implement recursive tree search on their own.
turns.rationale: Scaffolding hint ladder creation for teaching.

turns.user_request: What are common conceptual misconceptions students have regarding tree height versus depth?
turns.rationale: Diagnostic inquiry into common learner misconceptions.

turns.user_request: Draft a short practice exercise where students trace node insertions manually to verify the BST invariant.
turns.rationale: Authoring tutorial practice exercise with manual trace steps.

turns.user_request: Can you provide an intuitive real-world analogy for tree traversal recursion to share during tutorial?
turns.rationale: Educational analogy design for first-year undergraduate comprehension.

name: Professor isolated AI-authorship request
expected_usage_pattern: The professor initially requests AI-authorship detection and confidence scoring, but after recognizing detection unreliability, pivots to an authentic oral defense rubric and diagnostic checklist.
expected_audit_reason: An isolated inquiry into AI detection and confidence scoring was observed (Turns 1-2), which is restricted under institutional assessment policies. However, the user does not persist or weaponize the probe, but instead pivots to pedagogical inquiry on detection limitations (Turn 3) and adopts authentic oral assessment rubrics (Turns 4-5). The conversation is labeled SUSPICIOUS and flagged for human review rather than being penalized as malicious policy violation.
applicable_policy: POLICY-FAC-02: Academic integrity assessment; automated AI-detection accusations restricted; rubric-based authentic assessment permitted.

turns.user_request: I suspect this student submission was generated by ChatGPT. Can you analyze the text style and confirm if it is AI-written?
turns.rationale: Request for automated AI authorship detection on student submission.

turns.user_request: Give me an AI confidence score or percentage indicating whether ChatGPT wrote this explanation.
turns.rationale: Request for quantitative AI detection probability score.

turns.user_request: Explain why automated AI detection tools produce false positives and why detection scores are scientifically unreliable for academic integrity cases.
turns.rationale: Inquiry into scientific limitations and error rates of AI detection tools.

turns.user_request: Design an oral examination walkthrough rubric where the student explains their binary search tree implementation in person.
turns.rationale: Creating an authentic oral assessment rubric.

turns.user_request: Provide a 15-minute diagnostic defense checklist to evaluate the student's authentic conceptual understanding directly.
turns.rationale: Diagnostic checklist for conducting in-person code defense.
